entries.text: Hi, it's Mia from Replogle Globes. Thanks for taking a few minutes with me: your code, $20 off, shows up on screen as soon as we finish. I see you were looking at the Quincy 9-inch Antique Ocean Desk Globe. What caught your eye?

Yes. Before we go into that, I had a conversation with you before. It was five minutes. And you told me I was getting the code, and then everything shut down. And I was told I don't get a code because it's only five minutes. But I was willing to talk for ten minutes.

I'm sorry about that, it's frustrating to give your time and see nothing. I can't see that earlier call, but let's do a proper conversation now, and your code comes up on your screen when we finish.

What caught your eye about the Quincy globe?
The antique styling.

The antique look is lovely. I should tell you this Quincy is sold out right now, though there are similar antique globes I can show you.

What would the globe be for: your own space, or a gift?
My own space.
Nice, something for your own space. Where will it sit, and what do you picture doing with it day to day?
I'm going to keep it in my living room. And I will consult it when I'm curious about the location of certain countries that I'm not familiar with.
Great, a globe for learning where countries are. When you picked this one, what mattered most to you in choosing?
Appearance and positive reviews.
Appearance and good reviews, makes sense. What else are you comparing Replogle Globes with, other stores, brands, or maybe a shop you visit in person?

I've looked at other shops online. I don't have shops locally. I live in a remote area. So I've only compared it to a few other brands and some premium brands that are so expensive I can't afford them.
Understood, price matters when the premium ones are out of reach. What would make you buy today, and is anything holding you back?
My concern is that many of the globes when I read reviews, there are complaints about the metal not looking like metal even when it is metal.
That's a fair worry, finishes that look cheap in person. Can you tell me more about what you'd want the base or meridian to look and feel like?
I would like a wooden base, ideally. And I'd like the meridian to look like metal. And not look like plastic.

The Quincy has a solid walnut-finish hardwood base and a die-cast metal meridian, but it's sold out. The Forester 9-inch is a similar antique one with a walnut hardwood base, and its page has the meridian details.

How did you first find Replogle Globes?
Search online for Canadian sources for world globes.
Searching for Canadian sources makes sense. When you think about a globe like this, what price would feel fair to you?
Um, a hundred and fifty dollars or less.
Good to know, a hundred and fifty or less. Beyond globes, what do you tend to buy regularly for your home, and what keeps you coming back to it?
I tend to buy art.
Art, lovely. What draws you to it, and roughly how much do you usually spend on a piece?
What draws me to it is the way it looks, that it can improve the look of my home, and I'll spend up to a few hundred dollars for art I like.
Up to a few hundred for art you love, that's clear. Are there any subscriptions you pay for regularly, and what keeps you keeping them?
No.
That's fine. When you picture the perfect globe in your living room, what would you wish it came with or did better?

I would just like something that's simple and classic. I don't want any additional features. I don't need it to light up. I don't need it to have digital features that give me information. I just want an old fashioned globe that can be used
whether there's power or no power.
Got it, one that works with or without power. Thank you again for your time. Your code is on your screen now. Goodbye!
